Handoff doc below — normal prose, since it goes to other people.

# On-Call Handoff — Gateway 503 Incident, 2026-03-14

**Status at handoff:** ONGOING. Errors were still firing at the end of available logs (03:59:27Z). No recovery observed. Rollback not yet performed.

## Root cause

Gateway config generation 119, applied at `02:13:41.234Z`, flipped `gateway.pool.perRequest` from `false` to `true`. This disables connection reuse in the gateway's upstream connection pool — every request now acquires its own connection instead of borrowing from the shared pool. Pool size was left unchanged at 20.

At the gateway's normal request rate, 20 connections saturate almost immediately and are never returned fast enough. Every subsequent request queues on acquire, times out, and returns 503.

The config change shipped three keys; the other two are not implicated:

```
gateway.pool.perRequest:    false -> true     <-- cause
gateway.timeout.upstreamMs: 2000 -> 2500
gateway.log.sampleRate:     1.0 -> 1.0        (no-op)
```

Sole error signature in the log — 530 occurrences, no other error code present:

```
2026-03-14T02:14:18.972Z ERROR access  req-07401 /v1/cart -> billing-svc 503 659ms
2026-03-14T02:14:18.972Z ERROR pool    req-07401 ERR_POOL_EXHAUSTED acquiring connection from pool (size 20, in_use 20, waiting 13)
```

This is gateway-internal resource exhaustion, not upstream failure. No upstream service returned an error.

## Impact window

**Start:** 2026-03-14T02:14:18.972Z (req-07401), 37 seconds after config generation 119 applied.
**End:** not yet — still erroring at 03:59:27.974Z, the last line of the log. Minimum duration 1h 45m.

Pool state degraded monotonically and never recovered:

| Time | in_use | idle | waiting |
|---|---|---|---|
| pre-incident | 3–11 | 9–17 | 0 |
| 02:14 | 20 | 0 | 13 |
| 03:30 | 20 | 0 | 72 |
| 03:55 | 20 | 0 | 172 |

The acquire queue grows linearly with no drain. This will not self-heal.

**Affected routes** — all five production routes, hit uniformly at 106 failures each: `/v1/cart`, `/v1/catalog/search`, `/v1/checkout`, `/v1/orders`, `/v1/session`. Checkout and cart are in the blast radius, so assume revenue impact for the full window.

**Detection gap worth flagging:** `/health` continued returning 200 throughout, because health checks are cheap enough to win the connection race. Monitoring stayed green while all real traffic failed. On-call was not paged until `03:21:05.282Z` on `error_rate 5m avg is 71%` — 67 minutes after onset. The health check does not exercise the connection pool and should be fixed to do so.

## Roll back this deploy

**dep-4471** — gateway, 2026-03-14 02:12:00Z–02:14:00Z, author a.novak, summary "config: connection-per-request for pool isolation".

Action: revert config to generation 118, or set `gateway.pool.perRequest` back to `false`. This is a config-only change, so a config rollback should be sufficient and does not require a binary redeploy.

If connection-per-request isolation is still wanted, pool size must be raised to cover peak concurrency before re-enabling. At current traffic, 20 is not close to enough.

**Do not roll back these** — both landed after the incident began and are not implicated:

- dep-4472, billing-svc, 02:41–02:46
- dep-4473, catalog-svc, 03:20–03:25 (proximity to the 03:21 page is coincidental; error rate had been climbing since 02:14)

## Separate, non-urgent: worker latency drift

Not part of this incident, but visible in the same window and worth a ticket.

Worker job duration climbed roughly 11x over three hours, 200ms at 01:00 to 2324ms at 03:59. Workers themselves are healthy: zero errors, all 1080 jobs completed successfully, worker pool flat at `size=8 in_use=1 idle=7 waiting=0` for the entire window. Gateway pool exhaustion did not propagate to workers.

The drift is not caused by dep-4471 — it was already underway at 01:00, 73 minutes before the gateway config applied, and shows no inflection at 02:13. `db_wait` stays at 0–12ms even on 2300ms jobs, so the time is spent inside job execution, not waiting on the database or a connection.

Closest deploy is dep-4470 (worker, 00:48–00:55, j.tanaka, "retry backoff for webhook jobs"), which finished five minutes before the log begins. Plausible but unconfirmed — the log starts too late to establish a pre-deploy baseline. Pull worker logs from before 00:48 to confirm or rule out.

One unrelated known issue also appeared: `WARN db slow query 1.9s: SELECT * FROM orders WHERE status = ? — unindexed scan, known issue OPS-2210` at 02:36:22.838Z, single occurrence.
